securityNotices.count: {countText} {count, plural, one {time} other {times}} since you opened Cmdr

@securityNotices.count.description: Small line under a security notice that keeps happening: how many times Cmdr turned the same thing away since the app started. The notice updates this line in place instead of stacking new notices. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window. "Cmdr" is the product name.

placeholders.countText: How many times, already formatted with thousands separators, like 1,234. Always at least 2 when shown.
placeholders.count: The same count as a raw integer, used only to pick the singular or plural word.

@securityNotices.dismiss.description: Button on a security notice that closes it. After this, Cmdr doesn't show this notice again until the app restarts (it still records every case in its security log). VERB, imperative, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

securityNotices.mcpForeignOrigin.title: Cmdr blocked a web page from reaching the MCP server

@securityNotices.mcpForeignOrigin.title.description: Headline of a warning notice: a web page open in the person's browser tried to talk to Cmdr's MCP server (the local connection AI tools use to control Cmdr), and Cmdr refused it. There is no innocent setup reason for a web page to do this. "Cmdr" is the product name; "MCP" (Model Context Protocol) stays as-is. Sentence case, no full stop. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

securityNotices.mcpForeignOrigin.body: A web page open in your browser tried to talk to Cmdr. Nothing got in. If it keeps happening, close tabs you don’t trust.

@securityNotices.mcpForeignOrigin.body.description: Body of that notice: what happened, that nothing got through, and what to do. Calm, not alarming. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@securityNotices.mcpForeignOrigin.openSe.description: Button on that notice that opens Cmdr's Settings on the “MCP server” section (settings.section.mcpServer), where the person can turn the server off. Short control label; it may name that section. "MCP" stays as-is. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.tit.description: Headline of a warning notice: a network share (SMB) answered on a secured (signed) connection with a reply that didn't carry its signature, so Cmdr didn't trust it. "Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

placeholders.name: the share's name as Cmdr's volume list shows it, like “photos”

securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.titl: Cmdr refused a reply from a server

@securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.tit.description: The same headline as securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.title, for when the share's name isn't known any more (it was disconnected meanwhile), so it names the server that sent the reply in general terms. Sentence case, no full stop. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.body: The reply didn’t carry the server’s signature, so Cmdr didn’t trust it. A flaky network device can cause this, and so can someone tampering with traffic between you and the server. Reconnect, and if it happens again, check your network.

@securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.bod.description: Body of that notice: what Cmdr refused, the innocent cause (a misbehaving router or network device) beside the serious one (someone tampering with traffic), and what to do. Calm, not alarming. “Signature” is the server's proof that a reply really comes from it. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.rec.description: Button on that notice that connects to the share again with a fresh, secured session. VERB, imperative, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@securityNotices.smbSignatureRefused.dis.description: Button on that notice that disconnects the share. VERB, imperative, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.title: Cmdr didn’t install this update: it isn’t a genuine Cmdr release

@securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.title.description: Headline of a serious notice: an update Cmdr was offered didn't carry Cmdr's signature, so Cmdr refused it and installed nothing. It may mean someone is tampering with updates. Must read the same as updates.failure.notGenuine, the line in Settings > Updates & privacy. "Cmdr" is the product name. Sentence case, no full stop. Avoid the words "error" and "failed". Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.body: Every update has to carry Cmdr’s signature, and this one doesn’t. Nothing was installed, and your current Cmdr is untouched. Get the latest version from getcmdr.com, and please tell David: it may mean someone is tampering with updates.

@securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.body.description: Body of that notice: why Cmdr refused, that nothing changed, and what to do. "David" is Cmdr's maker, addressed by first name on purpose; keep the name, though in running prose it may take your language’s case endings or transliteration, like any personal name. "getcmdr.com" is the website address: keep it exactly. A "Send error report…" button sits below it, which is how the person tells David. Plain text. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.

@securityNotices.updateNotGenuine.openWe.description: Button on that notice that opens Cmdr's website in the browser, where the person can download the real latest version. "getcmdr.com" is the website address: keep it exactly. VERB phrase, short control label. Pop-up notice (toast) in the corner of Cmdr's main window.
